newsitem.title: USA: Elizabeth Taylor "doing fine" in hospital.
newsitem.headline: Elizabeth Taylor "doing fine" in hospital.

text.p: Actress Elizabeth Taylor was "doing fine" on Sunday, following a brain seizure that put her back in the hospital three days after being discharged following surgery to remove a benign tumour.
Spokesman Ron Wise said the Oscar-winning screen star, who was re-admitted on Saturday to Cedars-Sinai Medical Centre, spent the night at the hospital.
"She's doing fine. Her condition is good. She's very alert and whatever it was has passed completely and there's been no recurrence," Wise said.
Shirene Coburn, Taylor's publicist, said Saturday that the actress had suffered a mild seizure at home but stressed such seizures are a common side effect of brain surgery.
"She's up and alert, she's fine," Coburn said. "She's undergoing routine tests."
However, it was not clear when Taylor would be allowed to return home.
"I would hope for a short stay," said Wise.
Taylor underwent four hours of surgery on Feb. 20 to remove an apparently benign tumour the size of a golf ball from the lining of her brain.
Taylor celebrated her 65th birthday on Thursday, one day after she was released from the hospital.
